title: Conditions and subordinate clauses

objectives.can: Read conditions with הֵן, and clauses of time, cause and purpose.

explanation.summary: A condition in Biblical Aramaic begins with הֵן, 'if', followed by a clause whose verb is usually an imperfect; the result follows with no special word. Around it Aramaic builds clauses of time, cause and purpose from דִּי, from prepositions and from לְ with an infinitive.

sections.heading: Conditions with הֵן
body: Read Daniel 2:5 and 2:6 first. The king threatens: הֵן לָא תְהוֹדְעוּנַּנִי חֶלְמָא וּפִשְׁרֵהּ הַדָּמִין תִּתְעַבְדוּן, 'if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be made into pieces'. Then he promises: וְהֵן חֶלְמָא וּפִשְׁרֵהּ תְּהַחֲוֺן מַתְּנָן וּנְבִזְבָּה וִיקָר שַׂגִּיא תְּקַבְּלוּן, 'but if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive gifts, rewards and great honour'.

Each has an 'if' clause and a result clause. The grammarian's names are protasis (the 'if' clause) and apodosis (the result). The 'if' clause begins with הֵן. Its verb is normally an imperfect, and so is the verb of the result. The result needs no word like 'then'; its position after the 'if' clause is enough. A negative follows הֵן directly: הֵן לָא, 'if not'.

The 'if' clause need not contain a verb. In Daniel 3:17 the friends say הֵן אִיתַי אֱלָהַנָא דִּי אֲנַחְנָא פָלְחִין, 'if there is our God whom we serve', and then give the result: he is able to rescue them and he will rescue them from the king's hand (יָכִל ... יְשֵׁיזִב). Translators differ on how to take אִיתַי here ('if our God is able' is another common rendering), but the structure is the same: הֵן clause, then the result. The next verse, Daniel 3:18, says וְהֵן לָא, 'and if not' (that is, 'even if he does not'), and the result is a statement that the king must know: יְדִיעַ לֶהֱוֵא לָךְ מַלְכָּא, 'let it be known to you, O king'.

Daniel 3:15 is unusual. The king begins כְּעַן הֵן אִיתֵיכוֹן עֲתִידִין, 'now if you are ready' to fall down and worship when the music sounds, but he does not state what will follow if they are ready. He turns at once to the second condition, וְהֵן לָא תִסְגְּדוּן, 'but if you do not worship', and gives its result: you will be thrown at that very hour into the furnace. Translators usually supply a short result for the first condition, such as 'well'.

sections.heading: General conditions and לָהֵן
body: A relative clause can also state a general condition. In Daniel 3:6 וּמַן דִּי לָא יִפֵּל וְיִסְגֻּד is 'and whoever does not fall down and worship', and the main clause gives the penalty: he shall be thrown that hour into the furnace. In Ezra 7:26 וְכָל דִּי לָא לֶהֱוֵא עָבֵד דָּתָא begins with 'everyone who does not do the law', and then the result lists the penalties with הֵן ... הֵן ... הֵן, 'whether death, or banishment, or fine'.

The word לָהֵן needs care. After a negative it usually means 'except' or 'unless'. In Daniel 2:11 no one can declare the matter לָהֵן אֱלָהִין, 'except the gods'. In Daniel 6:6 the plotters say they will find no ground against Daniel לָהֵן הַשְׁכַּחְנָה עֲלוֹהִי בְּדָת אֱלָהֵהּ, 'unless we find it against him in the law of his God'. At the start of a sentence it can mean 'therefore' or 'but': Daniel 4:24 begins לָהֵן מַלְכָּא מִלְכִּי יִשְׁפַּר עֲלָךְ, 'therefore, O king, may my counsel please you'. Translators sometimes differ over which sense a given verse has, so read the whole sentence.

sections.heading: Time, cause and purpose
body: Time clauses are built with דִּי and a preposition. עַד דִּי is 'until' or 'while' (Daniel 2:34), כְּדִי is 'when' (Daniel 6:11) and מִן דִּי is 'once, after' (Ezra 4:23). A noun of time can take דִּי directly. In Daniel 3:5 בְּעִדָּנָא דִּי תִשְׁמְעוּן קָל קַרְנָא means 'at the time that you hear the sound of the horn', and the main clause tells what to do: 'you shall fall down and worship'. Such a clause often works like a general condition: 'whenever you hear it'.

Cause is expressed by כָּל קֳבֵל דִּי, 'because', 'inasmuch as'. In Ezra 4:14 the officials write כָּל קֳבֵל דִּי מְלַח הֵיכְלָא מְלַחְנָא, 'because we eat the salt of the palace', an idiom for being in the king's service, and so they report. The shorter word לָקֳבֵל דִּי does the same in Ezra 6:13.

Purpose is expressed in two ways. The first is דִּי with an imperfect. A negative purpose has דִּי לָא ('that not', 'lest'), as in Daniel 2:18 and Daniel 6:18. In Ezra 7:23 the king writes דִּי לְמָה לֶהֱוֵא קְצַף עַל מַלְכוּת מַלְכָּא, 'lest there be wrath against the kingdom of the king'. The second way is לְ with the infinitive. The sense is 'to' or 'in order to': נְפַק לְקַטָּלָה, 'he went out to kill' (Daniel 2:14); שְׁלַח לְמִכְנַשׁ, 'he sent to gather' (Daniel 3:2). The same construction also follows verbs of ordering and beginning: אֲמַר לְהוֹבָדָה, 'he commanded to destroy' (Daniel 2:12). The Peal infinitive begins with מ (לְמִכְנַשׁ), and the infinitives of the derived stems end in -ָה (לְהוֹבָדָה).

misunderstandings: הֵן is 'if' in these texts. A reader who knows Hebrew may expect 'behold'; the Aramaic word for 'lo' is a different one (as in Daniel 3:25, הָא).
A condition is not marked in the result clause. Do not look for 'then': the result is simply the clause that follows.
לָהֵן is not always 'except'. At the start of a sentence it is more often 'therefore' or 'but'. Decide by reading the sentence.
לְ with an infinitive is not always purpose. After a verb of commanding, beginning or being able (as in Daniel 2:10, יוּכַל לְהַחֲוָיָה, 'can declare') it completes the verb.

deeper.heading: The unfinished condition in Daniel 3:15
body: In Daniel 3:15 the king does not state the result of the first condition. Translations handle this in different ways: some supply a short result such as 'well and good', and others join the first half to the second so that the whole verse reads as one sentence. Either way the sense is clear from the second half, where the penalty is stated in full.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: The king answered and said to the Chaldeans: 'The thing is certain with me; if ye make not known unto me the dream and the interpretation thereof, ye shall be cut in pieces, and your houses shall be made a dunghill.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: הֵן לָא begins the condition: 'if you do not make known the dream'. The imperfect תְהוֹדְעוּנַּנִי is its verb, and the result is the imperfect תִּתְעַבְדוּן, with no word like 'then'.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, and bagpipe, and all kinds of music, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made, well; but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is the god that shall deliver you out of my hands?'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: The first הֵן is followed by 'you are ready', and the king does not say what will follow. Then וְהֵן לָא begins the second condition, and its result, תִתְרְמוֹן, 'you shall be thrown', is stated.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: וְהֵן לָא is 'and if not', and the result is the statement that follows: 'let it be known to you', and דִּי introduces what the king is to know.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Then said these men: 'We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him in the matter of the law of his God.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: לָהֵן here means 'unless' or 'except': they will find no ground, unless they find it in the law of his God.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Then Daniel returned answer with counsel and discretion to Arioch the captain of the king's guard, who was gone forth to slay the wise men of Babylon;
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: לְקַטָּלָה is לְ with an infinitive and states the purpose of the going out: 'to kill'.

practice.prompt: Which verb belongs to the הֵן clause, the condition, in this verse?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: But I have heard of thee, that thou canst give interpretations, and loose knots; now if thou canst read the writing, and make known to me the interpretation thereof, thou shalt be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about thy neck, and shalt rule as one of three in the kingdom.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

practice.explain: הֵן תִּכוּל כְּתָבָא לְמִקְרֵא is the condition: 'if you can read the writing'. The other imperfects, 'you shall be clothed' and 'you shall rule', are the promised result.

practice.prompt: What does וְהֵן לָא (words 0 and 1) mean?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

practice.explain: וְ is 'and' or 'but', הֵן is 'if' and לָא negates the case: 'and if he does not'.

practice.prompt: What does לָהֵן (word 12) mean in לָהֵן אֱלָהִין?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: And it is a hard thing that the king asketh, and there is none other that can declare it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.'

practice.explain: After 'no one is there who can declare it' the exception is introduced by לָהֵן: no one, except the gods.

quoted.english: that at what time ye hear the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, bagpipe, and all kinds of music, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up;

options: A time clause: 'at the time that you hear…'
practice.explain: A noun of time with דִּי makes a clause of time. The main clause is 'you shall fall down and worship'.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: The king answered and said to the Chaldeans: 'The thing is certain with me; if ye make not known unto me the dream and the interpretation thereof, ye shall be cut in pieces, and your houses shall be made a dunghill.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: The condition: if they do not make known the dream and its meaning
A purpose: so that they would not know
A reason: because they did not know
The result: what the king will do
check.explain: הֵן begins the condition and לָא negates it. The result is the threat that follows: you will be made into pieces.

check.prompt: What is the result of the condition הֵן אִיתַי אֱלָהַנָא דִּי אֲנַחְנָא פָלְחִין (words 0 to 5)?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us, He will deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and out of thy hand, O king.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: He is able to rescue them, and he will rescue them from the king's hand
They will fall down and worship
check.explain: The verbs יָכִל, 'he is able', and יְשֵׁיזִב, 'he will rescue', give the result. Nothing like 'then' is written.

check.prompt: What is unusual about the first condition in this verse (words 1 to 22)?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, and bagpipe, and all kinds of music, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made, well; but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is the god that shall deliver you out of my hands?'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: No result is stated; the king goes straight on to a second condition, וְהֵן לָא, that has its result
check.explain: The sentence reaches the penalty only in the second half. Translators supply a short result for the first condition.

check.prompt: What does לָהֵן (word 0) mean at the beginning of this sentence?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by almsgiving, and thine iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; if there may be a lengthening of thy prosperity.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

check.explain: Nothing negative comes before it, so it is not 'except'. Daniel draws a conclusion from the interpretation: 'therefore, O king, let my counsel please you'.

check.prompt: What does לָהֵן (word 11) mean in this verse?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Then said these men: 'We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him in the matter of the law of his God.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: Unless: they will find no ground unless they find it in his God's law
check.explain: The sentence is negative (they will not find any ground), and לָהֵן introduces the only case in which they will.

check.prompt: What do the three הֵן in this verse (words 16, 18 and 20) do?

quoted.title: Ezra
quoted.english: And whosoever will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king, let judgment be executed upon him with all diligence, whether it be unto death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: Together they give alternatives: 'whether… or… or…'
Each begins a separate condition with its own result
check.explain: הֵן repeated lists the possible penalties: death, banishment or a fine. This is a different use of the same word.

check.prompt: What do the words דִּי הֵן (words 3 and 4) introduce?

quoted.title: Ezra
quoted.english: We announce to the king that, if this city be builded, and the walls finished, by this means thou shalt have no portion beyond the River.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: What is reported, and that report is itself a condition: 'that if this city is rebuilt…'
check.explain: דִּי is the 'that' that follows מְהוֹדְעִין, 'informing'. The reported message begins with הֵן: if the city is rebuilt, then the king will have no share.

check.prompt: What does לְהוֹבָדָה (word 8) give in וַאֲמַר לְהוֹבָדָה לְכֹל חַכִּימֵי בָבֶל?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: For this cause the king was angry and very furious, and commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

check.explain: After אֲמַר, 'he commanded', לְ with an infinitive tells what he commanded. The Haphel infinitive ends in -ָה.

check.prompt: What does דִּי לְמָה (words 11 and 12) express?

quoted.title: Ezra
quoted.english: Whatsoever is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: A negative purpose: 'lest there be wrath'
check.explain: The king wants the work done diligently so that there be no wrath on his kingdom. The phrase begins the clause of what is to be avoided.

check.prompt: What does וּמַן דִּי לָא יִפֵּל וְיִסְגֻּד (words 0 to 4) state?

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: and whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.'
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: A time: after he has worshipped
A general condition: whoever does not fall down and worship
check.explain: וּמַן דִּי is the relative 'whoever'. The clause works as a condition, and the main clause gives the result: he will be thrown into the furnace.

reading.why: The king's offer and the friends' answer use the conditions of this lesson: two הֵן clauses in 3:15, הֵן אִיתַי and וְהֵן לָא in 3:17 and 3:18, the time clause בְּעִדָּנָא דִּי, a purpose clause, and the 'that' of knowing. Read slowly and mark each condition and its result.
